extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts for AMS journals using AMS-LATEX
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting manuscripts to American Mathematical Society journals using AMS‑LaTeX document classes, covering preamble, top matter, body, floats, bibliographies, graphics, and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the supplied template and appropriate document class
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the template supplied in the author package for your particular publication and the appropriate document class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the journal by the \\documentclass statement (e.g., \documentclass{proc-l}). Using the template minimizes production problems and unnecessary adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: File names should not exceed 20 characters in length, and consist only of numeric or unaccented alphabetic (ASCII) characters. Avoid overly generic file names such as article.tex, mybib.tex or fig1.eps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose distinctive, short ASCII names to reduce name conflicts and confusion during production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not modify page sizes or other dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not modify page sizes or other dimensions. Page sizes must conform to the specifications of the publication for which you are preparing your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text width is determined by the trim size; changing it changes line breaks (critical for math displays, tables, figures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not change default font size for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not modify the default font size, except temporarily for proofreading your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is [10pt]; using a different size affects line breaks. If used for proofreading, reprocess and check for bad breaks before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only public CTAN packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only “public” packages available from CTAN (the Comprehensive TeX Archive Network).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files must be processable in production; avoid nonpublic packages that production cannot access.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS classes already load common AMS packages
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the AMS document classes incorporate the code for the AMS theorem (amsthm) package and automatically load the amsmath package. The amsfonts package is loaded as well unless [noamsfonts] is specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not necessary to request these packages explicitly; consult their user guides for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not redefine existing LaTeX/AMS commands; use \newcommand
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not redeclare any existing LaTeX or AMS-LATEX commands. Use \newcommand, not \def, to be warned if the name you have chosen is already in use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid (re)defining one-letter commands; redeclaration can cause mysterious errors in output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place macro definitions in the preamble and use consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: Put definitions for frequently occurring mathematical expressions together in the preamble, before the start of the text of the manuscript. Once a macro is created for an expression, use it for every occurrence of that expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use author-defined macros in author names, titles, abstract, section and theorem headings, or references; use only standard commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid math in titles and headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the use of math in the title and in other headings. Titles are provided to online bibliographic services for indexing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TeX math coding (especially dollar signs) will result in inaccurate bibliographic listings and problematic PDF bookmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification numbers representing the primary and secondary subjects of the work and enter the information with \subjclass[2020] where indicated in the template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full numbers from www.ams.org/msc. At least one primary subject classification is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure graphics fit within margins and follow graphics guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure that graphics do not extend into the margins; check that all graphics conform to the AMS graphics guidelines (Chapter 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphics width may vary by journal; oversized graphics can disrupt layout. See Chapter 3 for file formats, resolution, color, and other requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use TeX coding to force line or page breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use TeX coding to control line and page breaks. Lines and pages may break differently in the published article from the way they break in the file you submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit break commands and spacing commands will be removed in production and can introduce errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation numbers on the left (AMS style)
rubrics_metrics.description: For displayed equations, the AMS style requires equation numbers to be on the left, flush with the left margin (default behavior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures predictable location and avoids interference with the QED box; using other numbering styles may be changed and could introduce errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \cite for citations (not in abstract)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \cite to indicate citations in the manuscript. The \cite command may not appear in an abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the standard \cite so that references can be processed and linked; abstracts must be self-contained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include complete bibliographic information; references may be enhanced
rubrics_metrics.description: Include all available information for references; use the abbreviations for journals and book series from [ABMR]. All references will be replaced in production by corresponding entries in amsrefs form drawn from MathSciNet (enhanced references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an entry lacks a MathSciNet record, AMS may update the style; report any errors to eprod-support@ams.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide author affiliations and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the research address or institutional affiliation and current address (if different) of each author. Email addresses and URLs may be included optionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses are part of the top matter but ordinarily printed at the end of the article following the bibliography. Do not include addresses inside \author{}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread and verify exact source matches accepted copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofread your article thoroughly and carefully. Verify that author-submitted source files exactly match the accepted reference copy of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production begins only after signed consent to publish is received; mismatches can delay publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of only necessary files
rubrics_metrics.description: Send only the files that are needed to process your submission or archive it for future reference (this does not include .log or .aux files, for example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple files, bundle them (zip) to reduce name conflicts and corruption risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred submission via AMS web server
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted electronic manuscripts can be submitted via the web server at www.ams.org/submit-book-journal. Submitting through the web server requires an AMS web account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors without an account will be offered account creation during submission. For email submissions use pub-submit@ams.org and include the journal code in the subject line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not load unsupported packages (list of problematic packages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some packages cause particular problems for AMS production and should be avoided (e.g., biblatex, epsfig, diagrams (Paul Taylor), geometry, microtype, parskip).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not load packages that aren’t needed. Use recommended packages (amssymb, graphicx, longtable, mathrsfs, mathtools, natbib, upref, tikz, xypic) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed nonpublic macros in preamble and permit independent processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Other macro definitions must be embedded in the preamble of the article file. Files must be able to be processed independently with all macros (not entire macro files) included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures AMS production can compile the article; use \newcommand rather than \def for macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS will add an AMS-specific hyperref
rubrics_metrics.description: An AMS-specific version of the hyperref package will be added by AMS staff at the appropriate stage of the production process primarily for the purpose of adding PDF bookmarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This will affect internal cross-references and external URLs; authors should not rely on their own hyperref settings to produce final bookmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive title and running head requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The first page of an article must contain a descriptive title. For article titles, only the first word, the first word after a ‘:’ and proper nouns should be capitalized. Supply a shortened form of the title if the full title is too long for the running head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague phrases like “some remarks about” or “concerning”. Enter shortened titles with \title[short]{full} and provide shortened author names in \author[...] if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract required and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: All AMS journal articles (except book reviews) must contain an abstract. With an AMS article document class, place the abstract before \maketitle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use \cite or \ref in the abstract. Suggested length: about 150 words for short papers, 300 words for long papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-page footnotes: subject classification and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Unmarked, unnumbered footnotes on the first page should include primary classification numbers (required); grant information (optional); and key words and phrases (optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting is automatic when using an AMS document class; give grant information using \thanks attached after the address for the relevant author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic data handling with BibTeX or amsrefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographies may be prepared using either amsrefs or BibTEX. If you are using BibTEX, insert the contents of the .bbl file into your .tex file; do not send the .bib file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biblatex is not supported. Enhanced references will be drawn from MathSciNet and may add DOIs and links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author addresses and current address placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic or other affiliations should appear at the end of your article, after the bibliography or references. A current address, if different, should follow the affiliation on a separate line. An email address should be included if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses are part of the top matter in AMS packages but printed at the end of AMS articles; do not place addresses inside \author{}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement is sent to the author(s) when the accepted work is received at the AMS. Production of your work begins once the signed form is received by the AMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors retain many reuse rights; details depend on transfer or retention of copyright and open access options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document class option defaults and cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of document class options: default paper size [letterpaper], [a4paper] optional for drafts; [twoside] default; version [draft] or [final]; default font size [10pt]; equation numbering defaults to left (leqno).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using [draft] marks overfull lines; [fleqn] gives flush-left displays; changing defaults affects layout—remove changes before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare theorem styles and environments in preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: To use theorem facilities, declare theorem types in the preamble with \theoremstyle and \newtheorem. Three predefined theorem styles: plain, definition, remark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Examples: 
ewtheorem{thm}{Theorem} or 
ewtheorem{thm}{Theorem}[section]. Numbering and shared counters are supported (e.g., 
ewtheorem{lem}[thm]{Lemma}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Top matter tags and required order
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the top matter tags provided by AMS-LATEX in the specified order: \title, \author, \contrib, \address, \curraddr, \email, \urladdr, \dedicatory, \date, \thanks, \translator, \subjclass, \keywords, abstract, \maketitle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every tag is necessary; templates contain the necessary tags. Some fields are required (title, author, address, subjclass, abstract) per the template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author name formatting and running-heading shortening
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter names with standard capitalization; use a separate \author command per author. If names cannot fit in running head, provide a shortened form in brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use initials for shortened running heads (e.g., \author[J. Smith]{Joseph Smith}); multiple authors may be shortened to 'J. Smith et al.' if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multipart surnames
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a multipart surname (e.g., van der Poorten), 'tie' the parts together with ~ (e.g., van~der~Poorten) so indexes identify surnames accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the tie (~) to attach a forename to the surname; automatic processing requires this for correct indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributors tag usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \contrib[...]{...} to indicate contributors responsible for a portion of the document (e.g., with an appendix by).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bracketed portion is required and gives the exact text printed. Multiple \contrib entries are combined automatically with punctuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \thanks for acknowledgments tied to addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the \thanks command to acknowledge grants and other support. Enter \thanks immediately following the address(es) for the relevant author, not within \author{}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each \thanks occurrence will print as an unnumbered first-page footnote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key words formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Key words may be provided with \keywords{...}, separated by commas, with only the first word and proper nouns capitalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key words are optional but help index and classify the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling and cross-referencing headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any heading may be given a label using \label{...} directly after the heading; references use \ref{...}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross references require running LaTeX at least twice; heed warnings about changed cross references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical text: use amsmath guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: For preparing mathematical text, follow the amsmath user guide and other standard references; use \DeclareMathOperator for operator names and proper math coding ($...$ or \(...\)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between roman text elements and mathematical symbols; code math expressions as math, and use \textup{...} in non-roman environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists and standard LaTeX environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow usual LaTeX conventions for producing list environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard enumerate/itemize/description structures as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AMS theorem environments (amsthm), not latex theorem package
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem environments following AMS style are defined in AMS classes and are incompatible with the LaTeX theorem package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \newtheorem declarations and the provided theoremstyles in the preamble; a starter set is included in templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displayed equations: alignment and break checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Check displayed equations carefully, making sure they are broken and aligned following guidelines and do not exceed the page width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-line displays use amsmath structures; ensure displays fit the publication width you are targeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roman type for labels and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers, punctuation, parentheses, brackets, braces, and symbols used as labels should ideally be set in roman (upright) type, even within italic theorem statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \textup{...} in non-roman environments; use upref or \eqref for roman references to equations; use math operator commands for functions like \log, \lim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercises environment: xca recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: The xca environment is encouraged for producing exercises that appear individually within a section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define xca in the preamble with \theoremstyle{definition} and \newtheorem; used like other theorem-class environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Floats numbering and separate counters
rubrics_metrics.description: Floats (figures and tables) should be numbered consistently throughout the paper; figures and tables are numbered separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbering should follow the document's conventions and allow reliable \ref references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Float placement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Floats should (1) be placed at the top or bottom of the page, (2) have an in-text reference, and (3) definitely appear within the same section as their first text reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A figure or table should not precede its first text reference unless they both appear on the same page spread. Allow floats to float (avoid [h!]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption placement and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions for floats are usually positioned above a table and below a figure. Use \caption{...} and \label{...} (label after caption).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caption style differs from basic LaTeX; caption packages may not match AMS style—avoid such packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use explicit centering in floats (AMS auto-centers)
rubrics_metrics.description: All AMS classes center the content of table and figure environments; using \centering or center environment is unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on class defaults to avoid inconsistent formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table width and rotation for wide tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure that the width of the table does not exceed the width of the text block. Very wide tables can be rotated using the rotating package together with the sidewaystable environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotate so the left-hand side after rotation is at the bottom of the page; set table captions above the table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics file formats and resolution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphics file formats can include EPS, TIFF, or JPEG for photographs; photographs must be at a minimum resolution of 300 dpi at the actual size that the photograph will be printed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not scale photographs in TeX. Color photographs must be saved in CMYK for print. For electronic-only journals RGB is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color graphics: CMYK for print, RGB for online
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphics intended to be printed in color should be submitted in CMYK format. For electronic-only journals only, RGB files are preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All RGB color graphics have to be converted to CMYK for printing; color reproduction may differ and AMS will optimize graphics for print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert color graphics to grayscale when printed black & white
rubrics_metrics.description: Color graphics to be printed in black and white or grayscale should be converted to black and white or grayscale before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check printouts on a black and white printer to ensure legibility; light colors (yellow) may disappear in grayscale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colored lines minimum width and tint
rubrics_metrics.description: Colored lines should be no less than .5 point in width. Colored lines in inherently light colors (e.g., yellow and cyan) should always be at or near 100% in tint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too-thin or light-colored lines may disappear or be indistinct in print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type in graphics: minimum point size and contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic type size inside graphics should be no less than 10 point at 100%. Do not put type on a dark background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 10-point type acceptable for print but may be hard to read online; check grayscale output for legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photograph file formats and color mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs should be at least 300 dpi at actual printed size; file formats can be EPS, TIFF, or JPEG; color photographs must be saved in CMYK format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not scale photographs in TeX; ensure sufficient resolution at intended print size.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEX-native graphics recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: For TEX-created graphics, tikz, pstricks, and xypic are supported; tikz is recommended for charts and diagrams and works with multiple engines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If code is short include it directly; if extensive (15–20 lines or more) place in a separate file and call with \input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling graphics with external packages: check margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages that apply labels to graphics ensure consistent fonts, but labels placed outside the edges can extend into margins or overprint surrounding material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If labels cannot be positioned inside the graphic boundaries, add extra space with \vspace to compensate and carefully check final layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced references and MathSciNet integration
rubrics_metrics.description: References in journal articles will be replaced by enhanced information from MathSciNet in amsrefs format, possibly adding direct links, DOIs, and standardized bibliographic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every reference has a MathSciNet record; the enhancement process may produce style inconsistencies—report incorrect MR numbers or errors to eprod-support@ams.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid caption and float options that conflict with AMS classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using figure or table options (like [h!]) or caption packages that change caption style, because AMS classes have preset defaults for consistent production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let AMS production staff determine final placement and caption styling to avoid pagination problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission contact and support resources
rubrics_metrics.description: If you encounter difficulties, contact AMS Technical Support (tech-support@ams.org or phone) or use AMS web submission help pages. For webmaster problems email webmaster@ams.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For TeX help, use CTAN, tex.stackexchange.com, and the TeX Users Group resources linked by AMS.
